question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool execution mode to agent-core, and should that mode require per-tool concurrency-safety metadata before any early execution is allowed?
rationale: The source-level gap is clear, but the fix changes core scheduling and safety semantics rather than repairing a narrowly broken existing contract.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep this issue open for an owner design covering early execution, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

options.title: Block On Safety Metadata
options.body: Treat execute-on-parse as dependent on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62962 or an equivalent concurrency-safety contract before implementation begins.

options.title: Defer Runtime Semantics Change
options.body: Keep current post-stream parallel batching as the only supported core behavior if maintainers decide early execution is too risky for now.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open for an owner design covering early execution, safety metadata, transcript ordering, hooks, approvals, cancellation, and regression proof.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest recent history across the agent-core runtime extraction, tool-call handling, and the current loop rewrite that would need the product decision.
